theory: Qualify the zero-baseline rule as applying to bar-height comparisons: a nonzero baseline is not automatically misleading for every graph, and truncation changes apparent relative sizes rather than necessarily stretching an absolute gap. Restrict the requirement to total $100\%$ to a complete set of mutually exclusive shares of one whole; percentages for overlapping categories or separate groups need not sum to $100\%$. Equal symbol sizes applies to repeated fixed-key pictograms, whereas proportional-area symbols require areas proportional to values.
